title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — Tempe packet taxonomic alias audit
purpose: Test whether the apparent scarcity of model descendants in the pass19 Tempe herbarium packet is merely an artefact of historical nomenclature. Current taxonomic backbones are used only as alias maps; they do not substitute for nineteenth-century labels or prove historical identity by themselves.

source_policy.taxonomy: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, Plants of the World Online (POWO) as primary current name/synonym backbone; ITIS used for Acmispon maritimus var. maritima where the current indexed Kew search did not expose the synonym list clearly.
source_policy.model_corpus: 05B_Blaschka_Digital_Archive_Literature_Technical_MASTER(1).json exact case-insensitive string search across the mounted full JSON.
source_policy.negative_rule: A zero string count is a corpus-search negative, not proof that no model, drawing or unpublished workshop reference existed.

audit_rows.current_backbone: POWO currently treats Brassica nigra as a synonym of Mutarda nigra (L.) Bernh.
audit_rows.guard: POWO's 2026 acceptance of Mutarda nigra is a modern backbone choice. It is used here only to widen the search, not to rewrite the 1892 specimen name.

audit_rows.current_backbone: POWO accepts Daucus pusillus and lists nine heterotypic synonyms.
POWO accepts Erodium cicutarium and lists Geranium cicutarium L. as its homotypic synonym, among a very large synonym set.
audit_rows.guard: The full POWO synonym set is much larger than the two names searched here. This row is not yet an exhaustive historical-name audit.

audit_rows.current_backbone: POWO accepts Cryptantha maritima and lists Krynitzkia maritima Greene as a homotypic synonym published in 1885.

POWO accepts Lycium fremontii; nineteenth-century aliases include Lycium gracilipes A.Gray (1877), Lycium fremontii var. gracilipes A.Gray (1886), and Lycium umbellatum Rose (1890, illegitimate later homonym).
audit_rows.nearby_model: model 343 is Lycium vulgare in the seventh shipment
audit_rows.guard: Genus identity is insufficient for a specimen-to-model crosswalk.

audit_rows.current_backbone: POWO accepts Eriogonum inflatum; Eriogonum glaucum Small is a later heterotypic synonym published in 1898.
audit_rows.nearby_model_or_drawing: 05B contains Eriogonum fasciculatum in the Corning drawing list and as model 580 in the 12th shipment, January 1896.

audit_rows.current_backbone: ITIS verifies Acmispon maritimus var. maritima with synonyms Hosackia maritima Nutt. and Lotus salsuginosus var. salsuginosus.

false_positive_control.05B_record: Corning drawing list contains Hosackia strigosa, 1892 or 1895.
false_positive_control.taxonomy: POWO treats Hosackia strigosa Nutt. as a homotypic synonym of Acmispon strigosus (Nutt.) Brouillet, not Acmispon maritimus. POWO also lists an illegitimate later homonym Hosackia maritima Torr. under Acmispon strigosus, which makes name-only matching especially hazardous.

stress_test_result.headline: Selective conversion survives nomenclatural expansion.
stress_test_result.finding: Expanding the pass19 exact-string search through historically plausible synonyms does not reveal a hidden one-to-one model pipeline for the Tempe packet. The strongest new outcome is methodological: taxonomic generic transfers can manufacture plausible false matches, especially in Acmispon/Hosackia/Lotus.
secure_model_descendants_after_audit: Hoffmannseggia / model 433 remains the only currently secure specimen-to-later-model branch in the minimum Tempe packet.
do_not_upgrade: Acmispon maritimus -> Corning drawing Hosackia strigosa

digital_completeness_guard.HUH_current_statement: Harvard's current specimen-search page states that the Herbaria steward approximately six million specimens, of which about 1.8 million are digitized and searchable, with new records added daily.
digital_completeness_guard.consequence: The nine-sheet Tempe packet is a minimum digital packet. A missing online result cannot be treated as absence from the physical Harvard collections. Collector-level completeness requires database assistance/export or staff inquiry.

article_consequence: The selective-conversion argument is stronger after alias stress-testing because it no longer rests on naive exact-name matching. The archive contains several tempting same-genus or historical-generic neighbors, but current taxonomic control shows that these should remain separate lineages unless nineteenth-century model labels or drawings explicitly join them.
next_steps: Request or derive a complete HUH collector-level result set for W. F. Ganong & R. Blaschka, 1892.
Inspect all nine currently indexed sheet images and record verbatim original label names separately from current HUH determinations.
Extend alias audit to the full eventual collector packet, using names actually available by 1892 before later synonyms are used as search aids.
Search the Corning preparatory-drawing list under both original nineteenth-century names and current accepted names, keeping taxonomic identity separate from document-title identity.
Do not change the public map from this pass.
